title: NGC 2040
caption: The nebula around NGC 2040, imaged by the Gemini South telescope
credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Image Processing: J. Miller & M. Rodriguez (International Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab), T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Wispy layers of red, orange and yellow wrap around NGC 2040 in this Gemini South image, giving the surrounding nebula the look of a rose in bloom. The object lies in the direction of the constellation Dorado.

NOIRLab presents this nebulous flower as an example of stellar life, death and rebirth. In broad terms, stars form from clouds of gas and dust, and massive stars live fast and die, returning much of their material to space. That gas, enriched with heavier elements made inside stars, can later be gathered into new generations of stars and planets.

The glowing layers were recorded through filters for hydrogen-alpha and oxygen ([O III]), which each pick out light given off by one particular gas. Gemini South forms half of the International Gemini Observatory, which NSF NOIRLab operates with partial support from the U.S. National Science Foundation.

understand.summary: Taken in visible light with the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on Gemini South through hydrogen-alpha and [O III] filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Narrow filters isolate the glow of specific gases, and the long exposure gathers far more light than the eye could.
